title: Spike: pure-Go SQLite under multi-process WAL (lang-council gate 7)
description: Answer lang-council chair condition 2 / gate 7: can a pure-Go SQLite driver (modernc.org/sqlite, ncruces/go-sqlite3) built with CGO_ENABLED=0 handle several processes writing one WAL-mode database safely? mattn/go-sqlite3 (cgo, real C SQLite) runs the same tests as a control. Brief: owner-approved plan 2026-09-25. Code on branch spike/sqlite-wal under spikes/sqlite-wal/, report docs/brainstorms/spikes/sqlite-wal.md; not merged to main.
acceptance_criteria: Per driver, 3 runs each of: 50x kill -9 mid-transaction (0 lost acked receipts, integrity_check ok); 32 writer procs + readers with a 5 s held write lock, busy_timeout 10 s (0 SQLITE_BUSY surfaced); concurrent 10 MB rows sha256 identical; TRUNCATE checkpoint under readers (bounded WAL, no torn reads); static CGO_ENABLED=0 builds linux amd64/arm64 + darwin arm64. Report has a verdict per driver with raw numbers and limitations.
close_reason: Revision 2 after GPT-6 Sol review (all 7 findings confirmed and fixed); report docs/brainstorms/spikes/sqlite-wal.md on spike/sqlite-wal. run.sh matrix: 108 result lines, 0 surprises (10 negative controls per driver fail/pass as expected). linux/amd64, 3 runs each: S1 50/50 kills confirmed inside a txn with uncommitted WAL frames, 100/100 SIGKILL, 0 lost/visible/partial, integrity ok via fresh verifier process; S6 (chair check 3 combined: 32 writers x 10 MiB line + 8 readers, lock held 5 s until all ready) 0 BUSY, 32/32 contended, 32/32 sha256 equal; S2-S4 pass (S4 allows writer BUSY, seen with C control too). modernc v1.59.0 meets gate 7 on amd64 and passed all scenarios under qemu arm64; ncruces v0.35.6 meets it on amd64 only (failed S6/S2/S4 under qemu arm64, cause unproven). Build gate partly met: static linux amd64/arm64 (no PT_INTERP), reproducible sha256; darwin/arm64 built, not run.
